title: qbmkit: a unifying open-source library for quantum Boltzmann machines

creators.name: Minervini, Michele
creators.affiliation: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Cornell University

description:
qbmkit is a Python library for quantum Boltzmann machines (QBMs). It is built on a single object, the parameterized Gibbs state rho(theta) = exp(-G(theta))/Z, and a single numerical primitive, the belief-propagation channel, from which every gradient and every quantum Fisher information metric follows.

It provides fully-visible, visible+hidden, semi-quantum restricted and evolved QBM models; relative-entropy, energy, likelihood, free-energy and semidefinite-programming objectives; arbitrary monotone quantum Fisher information metrics (the alpha-z family, which contains Kubo-Mori, Fisher-Bures and Wigner-Yanase) with quantum natural gradient; and six interchangeable backends behind one protocol: exact dense, thermofield-double statevector, JAX autodiff, tensor-network (purified MPS), quantum-circuit (with VarQITE variational Gibbs preparation and Hadamard-test estimators, requiring no vendor SDK), and imaginary-time Pauli propagation with a locally normalised sampler.

The library ships thirteen guided Jupyter tutorials, runnable examples, and a test suite of nearly 300 checks including paper reproductions, finite-difference and autodiff cross-validation, and cross-backend agreement.
